description: h² is an admissible heuristic for classical planning: it never overestimates the cost to the goal. It estimates the cost to reach each single fact and each *pair* of facts. A set of more than two facts costs as much as its most expensive pair. Because it looks at pairs, h² sees some delete effects: two facts that cannot be true together cost more than each one alone. It is at least `h_max` and is a good choice for optimal search on small and medium tasks, but its memory grows with the square of the number of facts.

papers.title: Admissible Heuristics for Optimal Planning
papers.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Planning and Scheduling (AIPS)

lineage.source: planning-heuristics, src/h2.rs: "The `h²` heuristic (Haslum & Geffner 2000): `h^m` with `m = 2`"; src/additive_max.rs names `h_max` as the case `m = 1`
